s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital renal and developmental disorder with multi-organ involvement and metabolic disturbances
salient_findings: Enlarged kidneys bilaterally with increased renal echogenicity
Significant developmental delay
Severe metabolic acidosis and electrolyte imbalances
Abnormal liver enzymes and bile duct dilatation
Abnormal brain electrical activity
key_facts: Prenatal ultrasound showed slightly enhanced parenchymal echoes and enlarged kidneys bilaterally
Born at term with normal birth parameters
Contracted pneumonia at 2 weeks
Admitted for shortness of breath and poor appetite at 3 weeks
Weight loss, dehydration, and hypotonia at 3 weeks
Required respiratory support through continuous positive airway pressure
Hypernatremia and involuntary eye movements at 4 weeks
Elevated serum creatinine, high plasma urea, hyperkalemia, and hyperchloremia
Severe metabolic acidosis with anemia
Elevated liver enzymes and thyroid-stimulating hormone
Dilatation of intrahepatic bile ducts in left liver lobe
Abnormal 24-h ambulatory EEG
Compound heterozygous variants in WDR19 and TG genes

shortlist.label: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Prenatal ultrasound showed enlarged kidneys bilaterally and increased renal echogenicity

shortlist.label: Nephronophthisis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum creatinine, high plasma urea, and hyperkalemia suggest chronic kidney disease

shortlist.label: Joubert Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involuntary eye movements, developmental delay, and abnormal 24-h ambulatory EEG suggest a neurodevelopmental disorder

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and thyroid-stimulating hormone, along with dilatation of intrahepatic bile ducts, suggest a systemic disorder

shortlist.label: Senior-Loken Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of renal and developmental abnormalities, along with multi-organ involvement, makes this a plausible diagnosis
